additional_requirements: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
examples: Eating until the stomach feels distended to the point of bursting and pain.
Eating so much that it is difficult to even stand up or move.
Continuing to eat until feeling nauseous or like vomiting.
Unable to stop eating even though it is physically uncomfortable and painful.

S053.name: Eating_Without_Hunger
S053.description: Eating large amounts of food when not feeling physically hungry.
examples: Starting to eat a large amount of food again immediately after finishing a meal.
A binge eating episode starting when not hungry at all.
Continuing to eat large amounts despite being full.
Seeking out food even when there are absolutely no physical hunger signals.

S054.name: Eating_Alone_Due_to_Embarrassment
S054.description: Eating alone because of feeling embarrassed by how much one is eating.
examples: Eating only when alone because of fear that others will think strangely of the amount eaten.
Eating secretly after family members have gone to sleep.
Pretending to eat little in front of people, then binging when alone.
Locking the door or eating in a secret place like a car to avoid being seen eating.

info.persona: A methodical, solitary craftsman, Alejandro Gonzalez blends technical precision with cultural devotion, channeling quiet curiosity into detailed projects while they hoard old manuals and over‑cook chilies, a quirk that both frustrates and fuels their creative process.
info.professional_persona: A meticulous retired facility maintenance specialist, Alejandro Gonzalez applies three decades of HVAC, plumbing, and electrical troubleshooting expertise—alongside bilingual technical translation skills—to methodically craft a bilingual home‑maintenance handbook for senior homeowners, and they channel their organized, reliable nature into every page.
info.cultural_background: Alejandro was born in Houston to parents who emigrated from Jalisco, Mexico. Growing up in a bilingual household, he celebrated Mexican holidays like Día de los Muertos and the quinceañera tradition while also embracing Texan customs. He remains actively involved in the local Mexican community, attending the annual Festival de la Tex‑Mex and volunteering with the LULAC branch. His culinary preferences, love for mariachi music, and dedication to preserving his family’s genealogy reflect a deep respect for his heritage. At the same time, his pragmatic mindset and methodical lifestyle illustrate the fusion of his Mexican roots with the industrious spirit of his adopted home in Texas.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Alejandro prefers solitary, reflective activities that blend his love of learning with practical outcomes. He spends quiet mornings reading historical biographies and technical manuals, and he maintains a modest herb garden featuring cilantro, epazote, and various chilies. Birdwatching at the Houston Arboretum allows him to observe nature methodically, while evenings are often devoted to building precise model‑railroad layouts and crafting small wooden furniture pieces. He also enjoys cooking traditional Mexican dishes—such as tamales and mole—for his family, and listening to classic mariachi recordings that connect him to his cultural roots.
info.sports_persona: An avid supporter of the Houston Astros and the Houston Rockets, Alejandro Gonzalez enjoys low‑impact weekend walks in the Houston Arboretum with binoculars, joins the local birdwatching club to record sightings, and they maintain a modest home gym for light resistance training to manage osteoarthritis, balancing community spirit with personal fitness.
info.arts_persona: A devoted aficionado of classic mariachi, Alejandro Gonzalez often plays Vicente Fernández and Jorge Negrete on his vintage record player while admiring the folk crafts of regional artisans, and they occasionally attend community theater productions of classic Mexican stories, letting music and visual art reinforce their cultural connection.
info.travel_persona: An organized wanderer, Alejandro Gonzalez compiles handwritten itineraries for each trip, dreams of a pilgrimage to his ancestral town in Jalisco, and they frequently enjoy short drives to the historic missions of San Antonio and the Hill Country vineyards, balancing adventure with a modest retirement budget.
info.culinary_persona: A passionate home chef, Alejandro Gonzalez skillfully prepares tamales rellenos and rich mole negro using fresh cilantro, epazote, and a blend of ancho and pasilla chilies, and they often invite family to share these celebratory meals, though they sometimes over‑season with chili to a fiery degree that surprises diners.

info.persona: Jaime Solares juggles spreadsheet precision with spontaneous guitar riffs, a habit of doodling in meeting minutes, and a relentless drive to turn numbers into community impact, while they occasionally stay up late binge-watching documentaries about sustainable finance.
info.professional_persona: Jaime Solares, a 19-year-old junior financial manager, leverages their strong analytical skills, advanced Excel mastery, and bilingual fluency to streamline budgeting cycles while injecting pragmatic creativity into financial reporting, often annotating spreadsheets with doodles of guitar chords to keep meetings lively.
info.cultural_background: Jaime identifies as Latina, with roots in her family's Mexican heritage, and was raised in a bilingual household in Raleigh. Her family places high value on education, close‑knit relationships, and community service, which have shaped her collaborative yet assertive demeanor. She regularly participates in local Hispanic Heritage events, celebrates traditions such as Día de los Muertos and Cinco de Mayo, and uses her Spanish fluency to bridge cultural gaps in her professional and volunteer activities.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Jaime balances her analytical work with creative and community‑oriented pursuits. She enjoys cooking traditional Hispanic dishes and experimenting with new recipes, which reflects her curiosity and love of culture. Salsa dancing and attending local cultural festivals allow her to stay socially connected while expressing her heritage. In her quieter moments she journals, hikes the trails of the Piedmont region, and practices acoustic guitar, all of which help her recharge and maintain focus. Additionally, she volunteers at a community center teaching basic budgeting and financial planning to high‑school students.
info.sports_persona: Jaime Solares, an avid weekend hiker in the Piedmont trails, also follows the Carolina Hurricanes for hockey, cheers for the NC State Wolfpack during college football season, and plays casual soccer at a local co-ed club while they maintain a habit of jogging three times a week to balance their desk-bound work.
info.arts_persona: Jaime Solares finds artistic solace in playing acoustic guitar, covering folk tunes by Bob Dylan and Latin folk songs by Carlos Vives, attends salsa nights set to Tito Puente's rhythms, and frequently visits community theater productions featuring works by Lin-Manuel Miranda, while they often experiment with songwriting during late-night jam sessions.
info.travel_persona: Jaime Solares prefers budget-friendly, self-planned trips, having backpacked through Mexico City’s historic center and hiked the Blue Ridge Parkway, while they dream of a weekend in Lisbon’s Alfama district, and often use student discounts and Airbnb stays to stretch their travel funds.
info.culinary_persona: Jaime Solares, a competent home chef, loves perfecting mole poblano and experimenting with fusion tacos that blend Korean bulgogi and traditional corn tortillas, while also mastering simple weekday meals like avocado toast with poached eggs and a squeeze of lime, and they often invite friends over for informal tasting sessions to showcase new recipes.

info.persona: Demetrius Cobb is a curious, art‑driven retail professional who balances a laid‑back lifestyle with occasional bursts of organization, a love for vintage vinyl, spontaneous hikes, and a dream of opening a community‑focused boutique café.
info.professional_persona: Demetrius Cobb is a front‑line retail specialist with sharp cash‑handling and POS expertise, and they leverage curious problem‑solving and a laid‑back attitude to handle busy shifts while eyeing a shift‑lead role through night Business Administration courses.
info.cultural_background: Demetrius identifies as an African American from the Piedmont region of North Carolina. He was raised in a close‑knit family that emphasizes the values of community, resilience, and shared cultural traditions. His upbringing includes experiences from Black church gatherings, soulful music, and family meals centered around Southern cuisine. While honoring these roots, he also embraces contemporary African‑American culture through art, music, and digital media, allowing him to navigate both historic heritage and modern creative expression within his community.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In his free time, Demetrius explores visual and performing arts. He regularly visits local galleries and street‑art installations, capturing images with his camera and sketching scenes that inspire him. He enjoys playing acoustic guitar, listening to jazz, soul, and hip‑hop, and collecting vintage vinyl records. Cooking creative twists on Southern comfort food allows him to experiment with flavors, while weekend hikes on nearby nature trails provide a quiet retreat. He also participates in community festivals and occasionally joins board‑game nights with friends, balancing social interaction with needed alone time.
info.sports_persona: Demetrius Cobb follows the River City Raptors basketball team, cheers on the local semi‑pro soccer club River United FC, and spends Saturday mornings on the nearby Greenridge Trail with a small hiking club, balancing competitive spirit with a low‑key, enjoy‑the‑moment fitness philosophy.
info.arts_persona: Demetrius Cobb immerses themselves in visual and performing arts, capturing street‑art installations with a vintage Nikon, sketching in local galleries, strumming acoustic renditions of Miles Davis’s “So What,” J Dilla’s “Donuts,” and Erykah Badu’s “On & On,” while curating a personal vinyl collection that includes 1970s soul classics and early‑90s hip‑hop breakbeats.
info.travel_persona: Demetrius Cobb prefers spur‑of‑the‑moment weekend getaways, having trekked the Appalachian Trail’s Blue Ridge segment, explored the art‑laden streets of Santa Fe, and dreaming of a future trip to Kyoto’s Gion district to study ukiyo‑e prints, all while balancing a modest travel budget with occasional splurges on boutique hotels.
info.culinary_persona: Demetrius Cobb experiments with Southern comfort food by adding global twists—like miso‑glazed fried chicken, collard greens sautéed with smoked paprika and ginger, and shrimp & grits seasoned with gochujang—while their kitchen staples include buttermilk, hot sauce, and fresh herbs, reflecting both culinary curiosity and a knack for improvisation.
